host: Yes. One command on a Linux x86-64 server with Docker
price: No usage fees. You pay only for your server
concurrency: As many as you set, within your server’s memory
takeover: One click. The agent waits until you give it back
sdk: A viewer SDK draws the screen and takes input; the buttons and prompts are yours
api: REST API with a token per agent
mcp: Built-in MCP endpoint, or on the server itself with no token; works with Claude Code and Codex
secrets: Text of four characters or more you type or paste after taking over reaches the agent as [redacted]; screenshots leave its results after a takeover, and password fields’ values never reach it
persistent: Logins, site data (caches aside), history and preferences kept between sessions, encrypted with a key your password unlocks; locked after a restart until you enter it; agents resume only the ones you allow
egress: No network of its own; your private network is off-limits
stealth: Real Google Chrome, webdriver false; clean on BrowserScan, sannysoft, rebrowser (Oct 2026)
files: Drop files right on the page, with real progress where you dropped them
picker: The page’s own file chooser opens your computer’s picker
downloads: Streamed into your browser’s Downloads as they are written, byte for byte; a page saved with Save as arrives whole, in one file
clipboard: Text both ways, with your usual shortcuts
recording: On the server in high quality, with your camera and microphone
switches: Input, clipboard, uploads, downloads, sound, recording; enforced on the server
proxy: A proxy you pick per session, checked before use, with its own time zone and languages (suggested from where it exits); name lookups go through it
port: One HTTPS port is enough; the media also take UDP where your network lets them; no TURN server
open: AGPL-3.0, everything around the browser (Chrome itself is Google’s)
